newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Fuel oil down on oversupply.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Fuel oil down on oversupply.

text.p: Front month Singapore fuel oil swaps were sold down late afternoon Tuesday on worries of prompt oversupply and the absence of support from arbitrage and crude players, traders said.
"Fuel oil swaps were over valued when compared to physical. The market was held up by paper players but now these buyers have disappeared," one trader said.
February swaps was last quoted at $98.00/$99.50 per tonne, down from Monday's $100.50/$101.50, brokers said.
The market traded earlier today at $100.00, $99.75 and $99.00 per tonne, they said.
March swaps was down slightly to $101.00/$102.50 per tonne, from Monday's $102.00/$102.75.

Traders said the market's weakeness was in part due to a $5.00 per tonne lost to fuel oil barge prices in the west and the narrowing of the fuel oil to Dubai crack spread from about $4.50 per tonne to $4.00.
"Paper was held up because fuel oil versus crude looked cheap and some people where playing the east-west spread," one trader said.
A trader said the market also lost some of its support as "most of the short covering is over."

The jet fuel swaps was steady after the early day's big losses in quiet trading due to market perception that most north Asia consumes have covered their winter requirement despite tight regional supplies, traders said.

The jet fuel/gas oil regrade for February was last quoted at $2.90/$3.25 per barrel down from Monday's $3.10/$3.30, one broker said. March regrade also narrowed to $1.80/$2.20, from Monday's $2.10/$2.40.
March regrade traded late Monday at $2.25 and $2.10 per barrel, brokers said.
February gas oil swaps was last quoted down 10 cents from Monday at $25.60/$25.80 per barrel in quiet trading. March was indicated at $26.00/$26.20.
